title: Alternative preparation of inclusion bodies excludes interfering non-protein contaminants and improves the yield of recombinant proinsulin
author: Mackin
materials: The frozen E. coli cells were thawed, re-suspended in 18 ml of BugBuster, 18 μl (450 units) of Benzonase and 0.6 μl (18,000 units) of Lyse-Aid rLysozyme. (BugBuster and Benzonase were from EMD Millipore, Billerica, MA and Lyse-Aid rLysozyme was from Semba Biosciences, Madison, WI). The suspension was gently shaken at room temperature for 20 min, subjected to approximately 15 s of homogenization using a Tissue Tearor homogenizer set at full speed (BioSpec Products Inc., Bartlesville, OK, setting “35”) and aliquots were taken for analysis. The sample was centrifuged at 8000 × g for 15 min at 20 °C and the supernatant was removed and discarded. The pellet was re-suspended in 18 ml of 50 mM Tris/HCl, pH 8.0, 50 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM EDTA, 5% glycerol and homogenized using the same conditions as above. The sample was again centrifuged at 8000 × g for 15 min at 20 °C and this supernatant was also removed and discarded, leaving behind the inclusion body pellet.

The reduced sample was subjected to buffer exchange using a 2.5 cm × 26 cm column of Superdex G-25 Superfine (GE Life Sciences, Piscataway, NJ) equilibrated in 50 mM glycine/NaOH, pH 10.5, 1 mM EDTA. The buffer exchange was performed at 2.0 ml/min and the protein peak was collected based on UV absorbance at 280 nm. The recovered, reduced proinsulin was diluted to 125 ml (approximate final concentration of 100 μg/ml) using fresh 50 mM glycine/NaOH, pH 10.5, 1 mM EDTA. Reduced and oxidized glutathione (Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO) were added to a final concentration of 1 mM each, the sample was briefly bubbled with argon, the reaction container was sealed and the sample was incubated overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Express and harvest BL21(DE3) cells
steps.instruction: Transform BL21(DE3) with plasmid hPI/pET‑9b, grow in LB‑Miller medium, induce protein expression with 0.4 mM IPTG when A₆₀₀ reaches ~0.8, continue culture for 2 h, collect cells by centrifugation at 10,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, freeze pellets on dry ice and store at –80 °C (1 L culture yields ~3.5 g wet pellet).

steps.title: Prepare samples for analytical RP‑HPLC
steps.instruction: For samples requiring reduction, adjust to 120 µL with 2.5 M guanidine‑HCl and 210 mM Tris/HCl pH 8.7, add TCEP to 7.5 mM and incubate 30 min at room temperature; add iodoacetamide to 25 mM, incubate another 30 min at room temperature in the dark; stop the reaction with 35 µL glacial acetic acid (final volume 180 µL). For non‑reduced samples, bring volume to 180 µL with water. Then add acetonitrile and TFA to final concentrations of 4 % and 0.1 % respectively, bringing total volume to 200 µL. Inject 180 µL onto a 0.2 × 15 cm Jupiter C4 RP‑HPLC column (5 µm, 300 Å) equilibrated in 35 % B (A = 0.1 % TFA in water; B = 80 % acetonitrile in 0.1 % TFA). Run at 150 µL/min, hold 5 min at 35 % B, then gradient to 55 % B over 30 min, monitor eluate at 210 nm.

substeps.instruction: Reduce sample (guanidine‑HCl, Tris, TCEP, iodoacetamide, acetic acid).
Add ACN and TFA to both, adjust to 200 µL.
Inject and run analytical RP‑HPLC as described.

steps.title: Isolate inclusion bodies
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen cells, resuspend in 18 mL BugBuster, add 18 µL (450 U) Benzonase and 0.6 µL (18,000 U) Lyse‑Aid rLysozyme, shake 20 min at room temperature, homogenize 15 s at full speed (setting 35). Centrifuge at 8,000 × g for 15 min at 20 °C, discard supernatant. Resuspend pellet in 18 mL 50 mM Tris/HCl pH 8.0, 50 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM EDTA, 5 % glycerol, homogenize as before, centrifuge again at 8,000 × g for 15 min at 20 °C, discard supernatant and retain the inclusion‑body pellet.

steps.title: Cleavage, reduction and refolding of proinsulin
steps.instruction: Suspend the inclusion‑body pellet (~0.35 g) in 2 mL water, add 8 mL 88 % formic acid (final 70 % FA) to obtain a clear solution, then add 0.42 g CNBr (final 400 mM). Incubate overnight at room temperature in the dark inside a fume hood. Remove formic acid and CNBr by rotary evaporation, leaving a white residue. Solubilize the residue in 10 mL 6 M guanidine/100 mM HCl, add Tris to 500 mM final (pH 8.1), add DTT to 50 mM and incubate 60 min at room temperature (take aliquots for analysis). Perform buffer exchange on a 2.5 × 26 cm Superdex G‑25 column equilibrated in 50 mM glycine/NaOH pH 10.5, 1 mM EDTA at 2.0 mL/min, collect the protein peak (UV 280 nm). Dilute the reduced proinsulin to 125 mL (~100 µg/mL) with the same buffer, add reduced and oxidized glutathione each to 1 mM, bubble argon briefly, seal the container and incubate overnight at 4 °C for refolding.

substeps.instruction: CNBr cleavage in formic acid overnight.
Evaporate solvents, solubilize residue in guanidine/HCl, adjust pH with Tris, reduce with DTT.
Buffer‑exchange on Superdex G‑25, dilute, add glutathione redox pair, argon bubble, refold overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Semi‑preparative RP chromatography
steps.instruction: After refolding, take 25 µL for analytical check. Adjust the remaining sample to 0.1 % TFA, 4 % acetonitrile and 55 mM HCl, bringing the volume to 166 mL (pH 2.0). Filter through a 0.45 µm polypropylene depth filter and split into two 83 mL aliquots. Inject each aliquot onto a 1.0 × 25 cm Jupiter C4 column (15 µm, 300 Å) equilibrated in 35 % B (A = 0.1 % TFA water, B = 80 % acetonitrile + 0.1 % TFA) at 2.0 mL/min. Elute with a gradient from 35 % to 48 % B over 40 min, monitor at 280 nm and collect 1‑min fractions. Analyze fractions by analytical RP‑HPLC, pool those containing proinsulin, and lyophilize the pooled material.

substeps.instruction: Adjust sample to 0.1 % TFA, 4 % ACN, 55 mM HCl, 166 mL total.
Filter and split into two equal portions.
Run each portion on semi‑preparative C4 column with specified gradient.
Collect 1‑min fractions, analyze by analytical RP‑HPLC, pool proinsulin‑containing fractions, lyophilize.
